newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-SWEDEN FAVOURITES TO CLINCH TITLE DOUBLE.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-SWEDEN FAVOURITES TO CLINCH TITLE DOUBLE.

text.p: Olympic champions Sweden will start hot favourites to complete the supreme double when their campaign for the world championship title moves into top gear on Monday.

"We have good chances to go all the way to the final," Sweden head coach Kent Forsberg said ahead of their clash with Russia on Monday night. The opening medal round match features the Czech Republic and the United States.

Sweden, gold medallists at the 1994 Olympics in Lillehammer, start the series in the box seat after beating the United States 3-1 on Saturday to start the medal series on four points, two ahead of a quartet of rivals.
Sweden, who last won the world crown in 1992, were unbeaten in the qualifying rounds and are confident of clinching a seventh world title.
"I have had such a feeling throughout this season. It is a feeling that has grown even stronger during this week," said Forsberg.

Sweden played in Turku, winning four matches and drawing one to top Group B and qualify for the medal series ahead of Canada and the United States. Canada, having beaten their North American rivals in Turku, start on two points.
"If anybody starts with four points it is a big advantage," Czech coach Slavomir Lener said.
Titleholders the Czech Republic, Finland and Russia won through from Group A in Helsinki, each carrying two points into the medal round.
"I am not all that impressed by the Helsinki teams," said Forsberg.

Relieved after collecting two vital points from a 7-4 drubbing of Russia on Saturday, Finnish head coach Curt Lindstrom said: "If we had had to come out of the round-robin groups without a single point to the medal series our chances to reach the final would have been gone."

Russia lost only to Finland but conceded 16 goals on their way to the final series. Lacking a world-class goalkeeper -- neither Maxim Mikhailovsky nor Sergei Fadeyev have starred -- Russia's success will rest with their defensive line.
The task will not be easy as two Russian defenders were injured against Finland.
The Finnish media have predicted a Nordic "dream final" between hosts Finland, the 1995 world champions, and archrivals Sweden.
Statistics show, however, that the Czechs loom as a real danger.

Roman Chechmanek leads the goaltending statistics after the round-robin series and all three forwards in their first line -- Vladimir Ujcik, Pavel Patera and Martin Prochacka -- are among the top 10 scorers in the competition.
"I am very happy with our goaltending," Lener said.
"Offensively, the Patera line has been producing (goals) in almost every game. In the final series we expect the other lines to produce as well," he added.
